feedback: Based on iteration 2's evidence, the increased sensor size and forward shift improved line coverage and early detection, reducing line loss events on oval and s-bend tracks. However, the slalom track still shows very low finish rates and relatively high steering oscillation, indicating challenges with sharp turns and control stability. If the next race shows reduced steering oscillation and fewer line loss events on slalom, continue with the current kp and sensor layout. If steering oscillation remains high, consider further reducing kp or kd gains to smooth control. If finish rates on slalom remain low despite improvements, try increasing sensor lateral spacing further or adding more sensors to better cover sharp turns. If line loss events persist, consider adjusting sensor forward positions or sensor size again.

reduce kp from 6 to 4 if steering oscillation remains high, as lower proportional gain can smooth control further.
